newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures close mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures close mostly lower.

text.p: April 24 - U.S. stock index futures closed mostly lower. June S&Ps steadily widened losses in the afternoon. Weakness in U.S. bonds led to profit-taking in the S&P pit. June S&Ps slipped to 772.00, towards support at 771.30 to 771.00. Fed's Meyer said U.S. economy was growing at an unsustainable rate.
However, gains in the technology sector were soon overpowered by the weight of the U.S. bond market, which resumed its decline in the afternoon.
The drop in U.S. bond prices reminded some S&P traders that U.S. interest rates could continue to edge higher in the coming weeks.

Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer's comments around midday touched off a wave of selling in the U.S. bond market. Meyer said the U.S. economy was growing at an unsustainably strong rate, with solid momentum continuing into the second quarter.
Meyer also said Fed policy should be pre-emptive, and that the Fed must be prepared to pursue a monetary policy that "leans against the wind."

In addition, a Japanese press report that Japan's Ministry of Finance was preparing an order to halt operations at Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co contributed to the bond market's weak tone, market sources said.
Meanwhile, June Nikkei futures widened opening losses and closed down 345 at 18,445.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps were down 3.85 at 776.35, KCBT Value Lines were down 2.40 at 686.00, NYSE Composites were off 2.45 at 405.55, Midcap 400s were 0.05 higher at 253.65, Nasdaq 100s fell 3.75 to 844.00 and Russell 2000s lost 1.20 to 339.80. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
